cases.name: a tombstone record entry
cases.pins: chapter 08 §8.4.2: a delete carries operation and deletedAt in meta and its signed payload as bytes

cases.name: record entries a reader cannot use
cases.pins: chapter 08 §8.4.2: no meta (a record pack written before this contract) or meta failing RecordPackEntryMetaSchema makes the ENTRY unusable, not the pack; the GET /sync/changes tail starts at or below its sortKey - 1

cases.name: a record entry of a type the reader does not declare
cases.pins: chapter 08 §8.4.2: an entry whose type is outside the reader subscription is skipped, as the GET /sync/changes tail would not have served it; unlike an unusable entry it does not bound the tail

cases.name: a record id containing colons
cases.pins: chapter 08 §8.4.2: idBytes splits at the FIRST colon; the signature covers the id, so any other split fails to verify

records.plaintextUtf8: a folder config whose path holds colons

cases.name: crdt_update entries of one document
cases.pins: chapter 08 §8.4.3: identity is the document id, sortKey the server_cursor, meta {sequenceNum, signerDeviceId, createdAt}, payload the stored packed envelope

cases.name: packed updates of a document purged at sequence 3
cases.pins: chapter 08 §8.4.3: a pack built before a purge still holds the deleted updates 1..3. A packed update is applied only above the floor read after the pack, at cursor + 1; snapshotMeta never stands in for the floor

cases.name: packed updates with a sequence gap
cases.pins: chapter 08 §8.4.3: the cursor stops at the first missing number and the reader pulls from it

cases.name: one update pair carried with two digests
cases.pins: chapter 08 §8.4.3: two entries for one (document, sequenceNum) with different digests make the document packed updates unusable

errorCases.name: header version set to 2
errorCases.pins: a reader rejects any version but its own

errorCases.name: one entry digest corrupted while the payload digest still passes
errorCases.pins: per-entry verification is NOT skipped when the whole-payload digest passes

errorCases.name: entryCount above PACK_MAX_ENTRIES
errorCases.pins: parsePack does not itself enforce PACK_MAX_ENTRIES — it runs out of index bytes first and says "pack truncated". A conforming reader applies the cap BEFORE allocating (chapter 08 §8.6) and therefore fails earlier, with entry-count-too-large. Asserting the reference message here would require deleting the check the chapter mandates, so only the code is normative
